rubrics.justification: The response substantially contradicts the provided laboratory grading of 3AA by reclassifying the embryo as roughly 3BC/3CB with poor TE and borderline ICM, indicating major morphological misinterpretation.

It integrates most relevant patient factors well, including age, BMI, ovarian reserve markers, endometrium, diagnosis, semen data, and first-cycle status, though the integration is built on an incorrect morphology assessment.

The reasoning is internally structured and mostly logical, but the prognosis and conclusions are materially skewed by the incorrect downgrade of embryo morphology relative to the known 3AA lab assessment.

Recommendations such as SET at age 30, not overreacting to one failed transfer, and no routine PGT-A after one cycle are broadly guideline-consistent, but the morphology interpretation conflicts with Gardner grading and leads to an unduly pessimistic prognosis.

It provides practical next steps for transfer, lifestyle, embryo selection, and future-cycle review, though some actions are less useful because they are based on an inaccurate embryo quality assessment.
